title: introduce-throughput-conservator-and-quant-wrangler-cli
author: Ayesha Khan
description: Context: Several tenants reported bursty traffic that caused head-of-line blocking in the continuous batching queue and unpredictable unit costs during surge windows. Independent investigation (ENG-8934) showed that aggressive batching plus cold KV cache misses amplified token cost during short spikes. Motivation: provide an automated runtime layer that (1) enforces tenant throughput targets to avoid catastrophic batch growth, (2) nudges cache prioritization for warmup-sensitive workloads, and (3) supplies a small CLI tool to produce tenant-specific quantization whitelists and compact quant profiles that respect quality budgets. This PR implements 'Throughput Conservator' (runtime controller) and a paired operator CLI 'quant-wrangler' (costctl subcommand) to generate safe quantization/priority defaults for tenants. Solution summary: - Runtime: introduce conservator module (infra/prefill/conservator.go) that observes request latency distribution and per-tenant unit-econ signals and applies a soft throttle that reshapes batch composition. Conservator exposes a small policy DSL (conservator.yaml) with: max_batch_growth, warmup_priority, and prefill_window_hint. It integrates with the existing batch allocator and KV cache scorer. - Cost tooling (CLI): add costctl quant-wrangler subcommand that: 1) ingests recent request traces and a small eval-set, 2) runs compact quant experiments (min-q -> high-q) with simulated unit-econ scoring, 3) emits a tenant-anchored whitelist.json (models + allowed quant levels) and a compact-profile.tar.gz for safe rollout. CLI supports --dry-run and --apply flags. - Defaults & rollout: provide a conservative defaults file shipped with the runtime (docs defaults/careful-presets.md) so newly onboarded tenants get a safe policy. The conservator will only enforce soft throttles for tenants above threshold (configurable). - Observability: add two new metrics: redwood.conservator.throttle_ratio and redwood.quantwrangler.safety_score and hooks for per-tenant unit_econ traces to appear in Console dashboards. - Tests: unit tests for conservator logic, integration smoke for CLI end-to-end local simulation, and a small load test that validates cost per token does not spike beyond configured SLAs. Commits: - "initial: conservator runtime scaffold + policy parsing" - "batch allocator hook and KV scorer integration" - "quant-wrangler CLI prototype + golden eval-set" - "e2e tests and telemetry + docs" Changed files (high level): - infra/prefill/conservator.go: new runtime controller integrating with allocator (approx 420 LOC). - cli/costctl/quant_wrangler.go: adds costctl subcommand with dry-run and apply flags. - defaults/conservator_presets.yaml: conservative policy shipped by default. - docs/cost-automation/throughput-conservator.md: user-facing guide and rollout instructions. - tests/prefill/conservator_test.go: unit tests covering throttle heuristics. - examples/quant-wrangler/sample_whitelist.json: sample output produced by CLI. Small code snippet (conservator decision heuristics): "if tenant.throttle_ratio > policy.max_batch_growth && unit_econ.delta > policy.cost_threshold { apply_soft_throttle(tenant, policy) }" Rollout plan: - Feature flagged behind runtime flag conserve_throughput (default off). - Gradual canary: enable 1% tenants -> 10% -> 50% with telemetry gating (look for no >10% regression in p95 latency and unit-econ). - CLI is opt-in; admin must run quant-wrangler and review whitelist before apply. Testing and results: - Local synthetic load: median token cost reduced 8% for spike-heavy workloads with negligible latency increase (+3ms median). - E2E staging: conservator reduced batch size variance by ~42% across synthetic surges. - CLI dry-run produced conservative whitelists that kept eval BLEU loss < 0.8% for most evaluated models. Risk & safety: - Conservative defaults and dry-run flow reduce blast radius. - Conservator uses soft throttles and falls back to policy-free routing if telemetry is missing. - Quant-wrangler includes a rollback marker in generated artifacts and integrates with rollouts/a-b. Related work: this PR builds on ideas from ENG-9021 (unit-econ instrumenter) and earlier prefill work (prefill heuristics). Links: Linear ENG-8934, ENG-9021, Support ticket SUP-7812. Merge notes: squashed commits and added final changelog entry.

review_comments: Ben Fletcher (reviewer): Nice end-to-end. Can we avoid global locks in the conservator path? Looks like conservator.go uses a per-shard mutex but some calls still hit a global registry.
Ayesha Khan (author): Good catch. I refactored the registry access to use per-tenant shard maps and a RCU-style swap for policy updates. Updated in commit 3.
Marisol Ortega (reviewer): The CLI output should include a safety_score and the eval-set used. Also add a note about encryption of the whitelist when stored in S3.
Ayesha Khan (author): Added safety_score export and appended metadata to the artifact. Documented S3 encryption recommendation in docs.

release_notes: Introduce Throughput Conservator: soft tenant throttling to stabilise batching during surges.
Add quant-wrangler CLI: generate tenant-safe quant whitelists and compact quant profiles.
New defaults and observability metrics for conservative rollout and cost telemetry.
notes: Feature gated behind conserve_throughput runtime flag.
Ops: recommend enabling on a small percentage of tenants first and monitoring redwood.conservator.throttle_ratio and unit_econ.* metrics.
Follow-up: add UI in Console to visualize whitelist differences and to preview safety_score per tenant (tracked ENG-9145).
